overview: A single index sheet for the State Department file on land and development policy in Formosa (Taiwan), listing three reports from Taihoku between September 1935 and August 1936. The entries concern plans of the Taiwan Government-General and associated development companies to encourage Japanese settlement in Taiwan and promote economic expansion into South China, the Philippines, the South Pacific, and the Japanese-mandated islands.

people.name: Maney
people.role: Reporting officer associated with the listed Taihoku despatches and reports

subfiles.title: Index sheet for Taihoku reports on Taiwan development and southward expansion
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes three Taihoku reports concerning Japanese colonization of Taiwan and economic expansion into South China, the Philippines, and the South Pacific.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists items 7–9 in the file, all associated with Maney at Taihoku. Entry 7, dated September 3, 1935, describes Taiwan Government-General plans for economic penetration of South China, the Philippine Islands, and the South Pacific, including a proposed Taiwan Colonization Company. Entry 8, dated July 3, 1936, summarizes legislation establishing the Formosan Development Company to settle Japanese immigrants in Taiwan and further expansion into the South Seas, while also referring to the South Seas Development Company in the Japanese Mandated Islands. Entry 9 identifies Taihoku report no. 43, dated August 12, but its subject description is absent from the surviving text.

interest: The sheet provides a compact guide to reports documenting the institutional and corporate machinery of Japan’s southward colonial expansion during the mid-1930s. It is particularly useful for connecting settlement policy within Taiwan to wider ambitions in South China, the Philippines, and the South Seas, and for identifying reports and legislation concerning several colonial development companies. The incomplete entry for report no. 43 also records the former presence of material whose subject is no longer given here.
